verdict.rationale: Gusto's own press release says developers and power users can install a Gusto CLI in one command or connect through its MCP server (gusto-docs-1). That is a first-party non-GUI interface, and agents can use it to prepare payroll work ahead of each run (gusto-docs-2). Beyond that single mention, the pack says nothing about running headlessly or in CI. Missing for 10: CLI documentation (commands, non-interactive auth, API tokens), any evidence of CI/pipeline or scheduled headless execution, scope of operations the CLI can automate without owner approval, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
